title: Introduction to Limits and Continuity
notes: **Meaning of a limit.** lim(x→a) f(x) = L means f(x) can be made arbitrarily close to L by taking x sufficiently close to a, from either side, without ever requiring x = a.
**Approach, not substitution.** The limit depends on values of f near a, so f(a) may be undefined or different from L; a hole in the graph does not by itself remove the limit.
**One-sided limits.** x → a⁻ approaches a from below and x → a⁺ from above; these are the left-hand and right-hand limits, written LHL and RHL.
**Existence.** A two-sided limit exists exactly when LHL = RHL = L with L finite; if the two disagree the function has a jump at a and no limit there.
**Continuity link.** f is continuous at a when the limit exists and equals f(a); limits are therefore the language used to define continuity, derivatives and integrals.
**Exam caution.** Never write x = a inside a 0/0 expression; simplify, factor or rationalize first and only then take the limit.
summary: A limit describes the value f(x) approaches as x approaches a, whether or not f is defined at a; continuity requires the limit to equal f(a).
